role: Author-observed source qualifications; independent review pending

issues.sourceObservation: The lecture models rotary DC-motor joints, not every robot joint or a universal second-order full robot.
issues.qualification: The bank preserves the model scope and distinguishes added electrical and flexible states.

issues.sourceObservation: The stator heading contains ironless winding while the armature description concerns a rotating current-carrying winding.
issues.qualification: Component-role questions avoid silently endorsing this questionable placement.

issues.sourceObservation: A high ratio reduces relative inertia variation only when the reflected motor term is significant; it does not erase the absolute load variation.
issues.qualification: Exact interval 11–15 retains its 4 kg·m² span.

issues.sourceObservation: Unmodeled resonances are described as very high and negligible.
issues.qualification: This is conditional on frequency separation and avoiding excitation, not universal for real mechanisms.

issues.sourceObservation: The half-resonance gain-selection rule is not a general proof of closed-loop stability.
issues.qualification: Questions explicitly label the design rule a heuristic.

issues.sourceObservation: The slide converts 60 rad/s to 9.7 Hz.
issues.qualification: The given mass/stiffness values imply about 60.0057 rad/s and 9.5502 Hz; even 60 rad/s gives about 9.55 Hz.

issues.sourceObservation: Equivalent factors 0.23m and 0.33I depend on the illustrated deformation assumptions.
issues.qualification: They are not universal constants for all robot links.

issues.sourceObservation: The controller uses maximum inertia then presents unit-coefficient error dynamics without explicit actual-inertia mismatch.
issues.qualification: Questions derive the ratio-dependent equation or explicitly assume matched inertia.

issues.sourceObservation: The normalized error equation labels the right side tau_dist without distinguishing torque from angular-acceleration disturbance.
issues.qualification: For an opposing torque d and desired-minus-actual error, the matched-model term is d/J.

issues.sourceObservation: The diagram labels a PID controller, while the later examples simulate specified torque rather than a demonstrated PID loop.
issues.qualification: No PID implementation or physical encoder test is inferred.

issues.sourceObservation: Imports, t_span, theta_dot_0, t_eval and plotting commands are absent from the shown code.
issues.qualification: The author reconstruction explicitly supplies imports, [0] initial speed and 0–5 s with 501 samples; these are not claimed as printed source values.

issues.sourceObservation: The plotted acceleration is formed with np.gradient, not exact analytic differentiation.
issues.qualification: The first endpoint estimate depends on the omitted time grid and need not equal the exact initial 200 rad/s².

issues.sourceObservation: The gear example rescales a no-load speed and full electromagnetic torque without resolving a loaded operating point.
issues.qualification: Literal code output and ideal transmitted-port arithmetic are kept separate from physical load capability in the presence of motor friction.

issues.sourceObservation: The eta-one curve is about 7 rad/s at 5 s while its legend gives the long-time 13.3 rad/s asymptote.
issues.qualification: This is consistent with the 6.733 s time constant, not a contradiction.

issues.sourceObservation: The final example changes damping and load parameters from the previous sweep.
issues.qualification: Its arrays use b_m=0.05, I=2 and b=0.2; tau_m=3 is assigned but unused in those array expressions.
